question: Which dance form in Manipur involves the use of swords, spears, and shields?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thang-Ta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thang-Ta** is a traditional martial art form from the state of **Manipur**, technically known as **Huyen Lallong**, which translates to 'the art of steps and lanes'.
 
• The name is derived from its primary weapons: **Thang** (sword) and **Ta** (spear), though practitioners also utilize the **Chungoi** (shield) and various other bladed instruments.
 
• It features two main components: the **ritualistic** aspects related to tantric practices and the **physical** aspects involving high-energy combat sequences, complex footwork, and athletic maneuvers.
 
• Historically, this art form was a vital defense mechanism for the **Meitei** warriors of the **Manipur Kingdom**; however, it was suppressed during the **British colonial era** and later revived as a performing art.
 
• The dance demonstrates the perfect coordination between the **shield** and the **sword**, symbolizing the protection of the land and the courage of the Manipuri people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ras (Manipuri Ras Leela)**:

 
 
• It is one of the eight major **Indian classical dance** forms, centering on the theme of **Vaishnavism** and the love between **Radha** and **Krishna**.
 
• Performers wear a unique stiff, cylindrical skirt called the **Potloi** and perform with slow, graceful movements.
 
 
 
• **Sankirtana**:
 
 
• This is a ritualistic performance involving **singing**, **drumming**, and **dancing**, primarily practiced by the **Vaishnava** community in Manipur.
 
• It was recognized by **UNESCO** in **2013** as part of the **Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
 
 
 
• **Choloms**:
 
 
• **Pung Cholom** is a famous drum dance where performers play the **Pung** (hand-made drum) while executing acrobatic leaps and turns.
 
• **Kartal Cholom** is another variant performed using large **cymbals**, emphasizing rhythmic precision and body balance.
